title: Rendezvous router rewrite, epoched KV compactor, and async-runtime upgrade
creator: Aditi Menon
description:
Summary:
This ticket rewrites the lightweight rendezvous routing layer that fronts the continuous batching scheduler, introduces an epoched compaction pass for the in-memory KV store to avoid long GC stalls, and upgrades the async runtime + transport stack to the latest supported release. The goal is to reduce tail latency caused by rendezvous contention and KV compaction pauses while removing technical debt from an old runtime and multiple deprecated crates.

Why now:
- Observability (console metrics + tracing) shows sporadic p99 spikes correlated with large compaction sweeps and lock contention on the rendezvous map during high-concurrency tails.
- Several downstream incidents traced to stale KV entries during slot handoffs.
- Upstream crates (tokio/tonic/prost) are multiple minor versions behind and block ergonomics and bugfixes (timeouts, keepalive).

Scope / Deliverables:
1) Rendezvous router rewrite: switch from coarse-grain mutex-protected map to a lock-striping + rendezvous-hash-based bucketed map with cooperative yielding. Add per-bucket watermark counters to avoid single-bucket hot paths.
2) Epoched KV compactor: implement a background compaction pass that compacts tombstones and stale slots by epoch marker, allowing short, bounded work slices and opportunistic throttle under load. Provide metrics (compaction_duration, compaction_bytes_reclaimed, compaction_pauses).
3) Async runtime and transport upgrade: bump tokio -> 1.28 and tonic/prost stack to compatible versions, audit all runtime usage (blocking calls, spawn_local) and replace deprecated APIs.
4) Regression suite and perf benchmarks: add microbench for rendezvous hotkey behavior, compaction pause measurement, and a synthetic high-concurrency scenario that emulates multiplexed chat workloads.
5) Rollout and canary: two-phase rollout with per-region canary at low qps, increased if no regressions for 24h.

Acceptance criteria:
- p99 generation latency reduced by >= 10% on benchmarked chat workload (same token distribution)
- compaction-induced scheduling pauses eliminated (no observed pauses >50ms attributable to compaction in perf harness)
- no increase in error rate (5xx) during canary rollout
- CI tests and regression harness green for 48h across linux-x86_64 and aarch64 runners

Design notes / trade-offs considered:
- We could implement a global lock-free map (epoch-based hazard pointers), but given timebox and maintainability we chose lock-striping + bucket watermarks to simplify reasoning and debugging.
- Aggressive compaction reduces memory footprint but risks longer pauses; epoched slice compaction mitigates this by bounding work and allowing preemption.
- Upgrading the runtime surfaced a couple of upstream breaking changes in our TLS/keepalive handling; we must validate gRPC streams under interrupted networks.

Implementation plan (high-level):
- Week 1: PoC rendezvous bucket map + benchmark harness. Open draft PR with bench results.
- Week 2: Implement epoched compactor, expose metrics and admin endpoints to trigger compaction heuristics.
- Week 3: Upgrade tokio/tonic/prost, fix compilation/runtime lints, run full e2e in staging.
- Week 4: Canary rollout, monitoring, on-call watch and rollback plan.

Observability additions:
- New metrics: rendezvous_bucket_contention{bucket_id}, rendezvous_yield_count, compaction_epoch_duration, compaction_pause_ms_distribution.
- Tracing spans: rendezvous.lookup -> rendezvous.yield -> compaction.slice for correlating with request traces.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: subtle timing bugs after runtime upgrade cause spawn semantics changes. Mitigation: run stress harness (100k concurrent requests) and schedule a thread sanitizer job for suspect code paths.
- Risk: compactor interacts poorly with snapshotting and lease handoffs. Mitigation: add integration tests that exercise snapshot+compaction and gate compaction when active handoffs are in progress.

Artifacts / Links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/89321/Rendezvous+Router+and+Epoched+KV+Compactor
- Draft benchmark PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/12345
- Runtime-upgrade PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/12410
- Perf dashboards (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/serving/compaction-and-rendezvous

Next steps / open questions:
- Confirm SLA thresholds for compaction throttling policy with SRE.
- Decide whether to expose a runtime flag to disable epoched compaction for legacy Dedicated clusters (compat concern).
